item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 241906
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
Issued by the NWS Weather Prediction Center College Park MD
200 PM EDT Thu Sep 24 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Fay, located several hundred miles southwest of the Azores.

Far Eastern Tropical Atlantic (AL90):
An elongated area of low pressure located a few hundred miles
south-southeast of the Cabo Verde Islands is producing a large
area of disorganized showers and thunderstorms. This system could
become a short-lived tropical depression or tropical storm later
today or on Friday while it moves northwestward to northward.
Increasing upper-level winds, however, should prevent further
development over the weekend. Interests in the Cabo Verde Islands
should monitor the progress of this system as gusty winds, areas of
heavy rain, and flash flooding are possible over the islands by
Friday. Heavy rain and flash flooding could also occur well to the
east along the coast of western Africa, particularly in western
portions of Senegal, The Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, and southwest
portions of Mauritania.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Roberts

item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Thu Sep 24 2026 
000
WTNT31 KNHC 242032
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Fay Advisory Number  19
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Thu Sep 24 2026
 
...FAY CONTINUES MOVING WESTWARD OVER THE CENTRAL ATLANTIC...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 PM GMT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...29.8N 41.8W
ABOUT 1020 MI...1640 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM GMT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was
located near latitude 29.8 North, longitude 41.8 West. Fay is moving
toward the west near 6 mph (9 km/h). A generally westward motion 
with some decrease in forward speed is expected over the next few 
days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts.
Some strengthening is possible overnight before weakening likely 
commences by Friday afternoon.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Forecast Discussion Number 19
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Thu Sep 24 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 242033
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Storm Fay Discussion Number  19
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Thu Sep 24 2026

Deep convection continues near and northeast of Fay's center, 
though the southwestern portion of the circulation is partially 
exposed.  There has been no significant change to the satellite 
intensity estimates, so the initial intensity remains 45 kt.  Fay 
has some chance to intensify overnight before an increase in 
easterly shear helps mix in very dry air outside the central core. 
The shear is expected to get fairly strong by the weekend, which 
should cause Fay to decay into a post-tropical cyclone in a couple 
of days.  No significant changes were made to the intensity 
forecast.

Fay's initial motion is unchanged at 270/5 kt.  A ridge over the 
central Atlantic should steer the storm slowly westward during the 
next few days.  Track guidance is in relatively good agreement, and 
the new forecast is basically an update of the previous one, near 
the Google DeepMind and HCCA aids.
